events_chronological: Over a black screen, emergency calls from inside burning towers are heard on the morning of a coordinated attack on the country's largest city.
Soon afterwards a source hands the agency the real name of a courier for the fugitive leader, Nabil Rasheed, and the report is filed away and forgotten.
Two years later the analyst Reyna arrives at a secret site overseas and watches her colleague Kessner waterboard a detainee called Faris.
Broken by sleep deprivation and humiliation, Faris gives up the existence of a courier known only as Sahim.
Reyna works the detainee network for years, chasing the name through interrogations on three continents.
Bombings in a European capital and at a hotel in the region go off around her.
Reyna's colleague Fay cultivates an informant who kills her and six others with a suicide vest at a forward base.
Reyna survives an assassination attempt by gunmen outside her compound.
A detainee's account is matched against the buried report, and Sahim is identified as Nabil Rasheed.
Reyna has the courier's mother's phone tapped, and he is finally located in a northern city.
Surveillance follows the courier's white four-wheel drive to a fortified compound in a garrison town with no telephone line and no internet.
Reyna insists the compound is the fugitive leader's, and the agency director demands to know how certain she is.
The station chief and the analysts argue the probability down to sixty per cent, and Reyna says one hundred.
The government authorises a helicopter raid rather than an air strike, and two stealth helicopters are prepared.
A special-operations unit flies into the garrison town, and one helicopter's tail clips the compound wall as it lands.
The unit clears the house floor by floor, killing the courier, his brother and one of the leader's sons.
On the top floor they shoot the fugitive leader dead and carry the body out as the crippled helicopter is destroyed.
Reyna identifies the body in a hangar at a forward airfield.
Reyna boards a transport plane alone, is asked where she wants to go, and has no answer.
nonlinear_category_reason: A decade told forward with date captions, whose one displacement is the report filed at the very start and left unread until the agency finds it.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs forward through a decade, marked out with place and date captions, and its nonlinearity sits at the edges rather than the middle: told-order bullet 1 is a black screen of audio from two years before the story begins, and told-order bullet 9 reaches back to a report filed at the very start that had been sitting unread in the agency's own archive the whole time.
fabula_notes: The buried report is described rather than dramatised, and its position at the head of the chronology is established only by the late discovery of it. Long stretches of the analyst's decade are compressed into captions, and the fugitive leader's own movements are never shown at all.
